# Run the assigned NCBI BLAST search through separately selected requests

Run the original sequence search and retain the information needed to monitor
and obtain its results. Keep the registered sequence, selected program, database,
hit-list size, scientific scope and caller constraints fixed. Choose the next
preparation, submission, status or result request using actual outcomes. A
different database search or a replacement sequence requires the responsible
parent's assignment; service transport does not make that scientific choice.

## Assigned request and actual operations

This resource uses service `ncbi_blast` in `api_service_assignment_v1`. Its
closed request is `{subject_ref, program, database, hitlist_size?}`. Program is
one of `blastn`, `blastp`, `blastx`, `tblastn`, `tblastx`; its required input
molecule must match the registered operand. An omitted hit-list size resolves
to 50 in the native command without changing the recorded original request.
The caller's configured NCBI contact and shared provider-access directory are
required for the actual client. Their configured state is information available
before choosing this service; a contact value is not a model-facing credential.

| Operation | Actual selected work |
| --- | --- |
| `api.blast.prepare` | Resolve and validate the original sequence/settings locally, without HTTP. |
| `api.blast.submit` | Commit the selected request and issue one native submission. Retain its actual RID and reported RTOE. |
| `api.blast.status` | Obtain one status response for that original RID. Available to result acquisition as well as the service catalog. |
| `api.blast.fetch` | In result acquisition, fetch one native JSON2 response for the original RID. It performs no preliminary status poll or waiting loop. |

Each operation takes empty arguments and uses the original assignment/handle.
Submission includes operand resolution; a separate prepare action is useful
when its information informs the next choice, not a required first stage.
Results use empty native selector `{}`. Choosing a status observation and
choosing result retrieval are separate actions; the parent need not commission
another monitor before results acquisition can inspect readiness.

## Provider constraints and uncertain outcomes

NCBI's Common URL API uses `CMD=Put` to submit and `CMD=Get` with the returned
RID for status or retrieval. Retain the native response before interpreting it.
RTOE is the service's reported estimate, not a validated remaining duration or a
mandatory wait chosen by infrastructure. Preserve `WAITING`, `READY`, `FAILED`
and `UNKNOWN` without inventing queue position, throughput or completion fraction.
`WAITING` establishes an accepted unfinished search, not that native execution
has begun. `READY` can legitimately report no hits.

NCBI requires at least ten seconds between service contacts and at least sixty
seconds between polls of one RID. The client returns earliest-permitted timing
or explicit spacing feedback; no primitive sleeps or polls automatically. Use
those factual limits when choosing a permitted request, another useful action
or an available explicit wait. They are not a fixed episode polling cadence.

An unknown submission outcome is not proof that no job exists. Preserve the
original intent, response, handle and specific failure. Recovery does not repeat
the POST. A confirmed local not-sent failure and an uncertain remote submission
are different facts; the episode and parent need that distinction for repair.
An observation failure is not evidence that the search failed.

## Handoff, native results and interpretation

A validated original RID establishes the usable monitoring/results handoff;
the search may still be unfinished. Validated completion immediately sets this
practical assignment's future expected credit to zero, retaining the final
actual gain. Monitoring and results operate independently on that same work.

Result publication requires the original actual submission response and matching
query/program identity. A READY status response is protocol information, not a
scientific result payload. Fetch retains the original JSON2/archive bytes and
native member bytes, reported program version, requested/effective database,
reference subjects, HSP scores, E-values, alignments and coordinate units. Native
database alias resolution remains reported source information; it is not a
silent change by episode infrastructure. Keep valid HSPs and their source when
another HSP cannot be projected. A native no-hit result is scoped to this
submitted operand and recorded search settings, not biological absence.

The scientific parent interprets sequence evidence and its transfer limits.
Acquisition assigns neither function nor lineage. Source custody, operational
progress, duration measurements and scientific annotation support remain
separate. Repeated publication does not repeat the physical search or add new
credit for the same content.

- [NCBI BLAST Common URL API](https://blast.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/doc/blast-help/urlapi.html).
- Actual bindings: `api_blast.py`, the single-request `PublicClients.blast`,
  `blast_search.py` and native publication in `tools.py`. The API episode does
  not wrap the older `RemoteSearches.search/collect` polling loop.

parent's assignment; service transport does not make that scientific choice.

## Assigned request and actual operations

This resource uses service `ncbi_blast` in `api_service_assignment_v1`. Its
closed request is `{subject_ref, program, database, hitlist_size?}`. Program is
one of `blastn`, `blastp`, `blastx`, `tblastn`, `tblastx`; its required input
molecule must match the registered operand. An omitted hit-list size resolves
to 50 in the native command without changing the recorded original request.
The caller's configured NCBI contact and shared provider-access directory are
required for the actual client. Their configured state is information available
before choosing this service; a contact value is not a model-facing credential.

| Operation | Actual selected work |
| --- | --- |
| `api.blast.prepare` | Resolve and validate the original sequence/settings locally, without HTTP. |
| `api.blast.submit` | Commit the selected request and issue one native submission. Retain its actual RID and reported RTOE. |
| `api.blast.status` | Obtain one status response for that original RID. Available to result acquisition as well as the service catalog. |
| `api.blast.fetch` | In result acquisition, fetch one native JSON2 response for the original RID. It performs no preliminary status poll or waiting loop. |

Each operation takes empty arguments and uses the original assignment/handle.
Submission includes operand resolution; a separate prepare action is useful
when its information informs the next choice, not a required first stage.
Results use empty native selector `{}`. Choosing a status observation and
choosing result retrieval are separate actions; the parent need not commission
another monitor before results acquisition can inspect readiness.

## Provider constraints and uncertain outcomes

NCBI's Common URL API uses `CMD=Put` to submit and `CMD=Get` with the returned
RID for status or retrieval. Retain the native response before interpreting it.
RTOE is the service's reported estimate, not a validated remaining duration or a
mandatory wait chosen by infrastructure. Preserve `WAITING`, `READY`, `FAILED`
and `UNKNOWN` without inventing queue position, throughput or completion fraction.
`WAITING` establishes an accepted unfinished search, not that native execution
has begun. `READY` can legitimately report no hits.

NCBI requires at least ten seconds between service contacts and at least sixty
seconds between polls of one RID. The client returns earliest-permitted timing
or explicit spacing feedback; no primitive sleeps or polls automatically. Use
those factual limits when choosing a permitted request, another useful action
or an available explicit wait. They are not a fixed episode polling cadence.

An unknown submission outcome is not proof that no job exists. Preserve the
original intent, response, handle and specific failure. Recovery does not repeat
the POST. A confirmed local not-sent failure and an uncertain remote submission
are different facts; the episode and parent need that distinction for repair.
An observation failure is not evidence that the search failed.

## Handoff, native results and interpretation

A validated original RID establishes the usable monitoring/results handoff;
the search may still be unfinished. Validated completion immediately sets this
practical assignment's future expected credit to zero, retaining the final
actual gain. Monitoring and results operate independently on that same work.

Result publication requires the original actual submission response and matching
query/program identity. A READY status response is protocol information, not a
scientific result payload. Fetch retains the original JSON2/archive bytes and
native member bytes, reported program version, requested/effective database,
reference subjects, HSP scores, E-values, alignments and coordinate units. Native
database alias resolution remains reported source information; it is not a
silent change by episode infrastructure. Keep valid HSPs and their source when
another HSP cannot be projected. A native no-hit result is scoped to this
submitted operand and recorded search settings, not biological absence.

The scientific parent interprets sequence evidence and its transfer limits.
Acquisition assigns neither function nor lineage. Source custody, operational
progress, duration measurements and scientific annotation support remain
separate. Repeated publication does not repeat the physical search or add new
credit for the same content.

# Retrieve the assigned BV-BRC Data API v2 measurements and source records

Use the parent's selected collection, typed predicates and requested result
projection to acquire annotation-relevant molecular data. The parent supplies
the job, scope, constraints and typed return; the assigned API and results
episodes choose their next permitted operations. These are tool instructions,
not a complete episode or a scoring rubric.

The service is `bvbrc_data`, using the caller-configured Data API base URL and
timeout. Its default base URL is `https://www.bv-brc.org/api`. The resource is
`api`; the local HTTP client does not establish local scientific computation or
an HPC deployment. This provider performs public unauthenticated Data API GETs.
Its configuration establishes a route, not current service availability or
access to private data. BV-BRC AppService computation, task submission and
Workspace transfer are separate capabilities not supplied by these operations.

## Actual operations and their owners

| Operation | Callable arguments | Assigned work and result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `api.bvbrc.data.query` | `{}` | The assigned `launch_api` child executes exactly one prepared v2 page, count or facet GET and retains its response as the original handoff. |
| `api.bvbrc.data.result` | `{}` | The assigned `results` child obtains the selected response, retains its complete raw bytes and populated numerical sheet, and applies the frozen local projection and explicit supplied-input joins. |

The request and selector belong in the existing launch/results assignments,
not in these empty operation arguments. Reading or selecting this information
does not enable direct invocation from a scientific parent. The actual
configured resource contracts determine the commission route.

A Data API response is immediate. There is no remote task identifier, queue,
submission, status-poll operation or compulsory monitoring itinerary. Existing
monitoring observes the original retained response at its original observation
time; it does not make a fresh GET or invent execution-duration measurements.

## Select a collection and typed query

The request has version `bvbrc_data_request_v2`, one explicit `collection`,
`mode` (`page`, `count` or `facet`), and an array of `filters` combined with AND.
The 22 supported collection names are:

| Data | Collections |
| --- | --- |
| Sequences and genomic context | `genome`, `genome_feature`, `genome_sequence`, `feature_sequence` |
| Functions, domains and sequence features | `protein_family_ref`, `protein_feature`, `sequence_feature`, `sequence_feature_vt`, `structured_assertion` |
| Identifiers and taxonomy | `id_ref`, `taxonomy` |
| Pathways and functional vocabulary | `pathway`, `pathway_ref`, `subsystem`, `subsystem_ref`, `enzyme_class_ref`, `gene_ontology_ref` |
| Molecular structures and interactions | `protein_structure`, `ppi` |
| Molecular experiments | `experiment`, `bioset`, `bioset_result` |

Use the reviewed fields and native types in the supplied request contract.
Unknown fields are explicit errors; validation does not discover schemas or
guess a collection. Work can start from a supplied sequence or file contents.
For example, an explicitly obtained sequence MD5 can identify matching
`aa_sequence_md5` or `na_sequence_md5` memberships in `genome_feature`, followed
by an explicitly selected sequence join. No candidate annotation or searchable
gene name is required. A source's product label remains its assertion about
that source record.

| Predicate | Required operands and meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `eq` | `{field, operator: eq, value}`; exact typed equality on a supported field. |
| `in` | `{field, operator: in, value: [...]}`; a nonempty array of values of the field's type; a match to any member satisfies this predicate. |
| `range` | `{field, operator: range, lower, lower_inclusive, upper, upper_inclusive}`; numeric bounds with explicit inclusivity. At least one bound is present; a null bound requires its inclusivity flag to be false. |
| `exists` | `{field, operator: exists, present}`; explicitly require presence or absence of an indexed field. |

Scalar predicates on a multivalued field mean document membership. Numeric
strings and booleans are not numbers; integer fields require integers. Exact
matching on analyzed text fields and date ranges are unsupported. Reversed
bounds, unregistered fields and unsupported sorting/faceting are rejected.
Literal punctuation is escaped by the pure query compiler; supply literal
values, never raw Solr/RQL fragments, URLs or HTTP instructions.

For `page`, optional `fields` is a nonempty unique list; omission selects only
the collection's unique key. The effective request adds that key to an explicit
field list when necessary for record identity. Optional `sort` contains
`{field, direction: asc|desc}` entries. Omitted/empty sorting uses the unique key
ascending; a supplied order gains that tie breaker only when absent. Defaults
are `offset=0` and `limit=25`; page limit is 1 through 25,000. Original omissions
and separately resolved defaults/additions are retained. Stable sorting does
not make separate requests an atomic database snapshot.

`count` rejects row fields, sorting, offset and limit. `facet` also rejects
those row-page operands and requires exactly
`{field, offset, limit, min_count, sort: index|count, include_missing}` in
`facet`. Its bucket offset/limit are distinct from document pagination. Both
count and facet request zero document rows; a count of two with zero returned
documents is a valid count result. Changing filters, collection, mode or a facet
window requires another explicitly assigned query.

The prepared profile is `solr_query_solr_json_v1`: one GET with
`Content-Type: application/solrquery+x-www-form-urlencoded` and
`Accept: application/solr+json`. The parser expects a `solr_json_envelope_v1`
response. A JSON row array or a `.json` suffix does not establish that profile.
The actual prepared request is persisted; recovery and publication use it
without recompiling historical work with today's compiler.

## Freeze the requested result projection and explicit inputs

The results selector is a closed `bvbrc_data_result_selector_v2` record with
all five keys: `version`, `page`, `projection`, `inputs`, `supplied_metadata`.
For page mode, `page` is null to retain the original page, or exactly
`{offset, limit}`. Count/facet require null. An unchanged effective native page
reuses the original response with no HTTP request; an explicitly changed page
makes one GET. There is no automatic next-page retrieval, retry or redirect.

Select one projection family:

| Family | Explicit selection |
| --- | --- |
| `query_metadata` | Page/count/facet metadata for the original query population; no row selection or additional inputs. |
| `collection_rows` | Native `row_indices`, `numeric_fields` and `metadata_fields` from this acquired page; no additional inputs. |
| `feature_sequence` | `feature_ids`, `sequence_kind: AA|NA`, `include_sequence_values` and `feature_metadata_fields`, using selected `genome_feature` and `feature_sequence` pages. |
| `molecular_experiment` | `result_ids`, `measurement_fields` and source-level `metadata_fields`, using selected `bioset_result`, `bioset`, `experiment` and `genome_feature` pages and optional supplied metadata. |

The current page participates under its actual collection. Every additional
page is an explicit `{collection, source_ref}` in `inputs` and must already be
received by the assigning episode. A same-scope source or matching provider
label alone is insufficient. Supplied metadata identifies its received JSON
source and exact JSON Pointer; the host verifies that the pointed object equals
the supplied values. It does not create a BV-BRC native checksum for those
values. No parser, extractor or calculator acquires a missing page or metadata.

Feature joins retain each feature occurrence, its AA/NA MD5 and the corresponding
sequence record. Shared sequences do not merge distinct features. Molecular
joins preserve result, bioset, experiment and feature/entity relationships,
conditions, units and explicitly supplied sample/replicate design. Missing or
ambiguous joins remain qualified unavailable results or explicit conflicts.

## Native quantities, deterministic functions and missing data

`bvbrc_data_readers.parse_data_snapshot` populates native rows, typed cells,
numerical cells and page/count/facet qualifications from the retained response
and persisted prepared request. The publisher separately invokes
`bvbrc_data_calculators.calculate_page_counts`, and for facets
`calculate_facet_fractions` with
`denominator_policy="same_response_exact_document_count"`. A facet fraction is
the native bucket count divided by the same response's exact matching-document
count; an unknown, inexact or zero denominator gives an unavailable fraction,
not zero. Multivalued buckets can overlap and need not sum to one. A limited
bucket window or a single page does not describe the complete population.

The feature projection uses
`bvbrc_data_feature_sequences.extract_feature_sequence_join` and the separate
`calculate_feature_sequence_counts`. The molecular projection uses
`bvbrc_data_molecular.extract_molecular_experiment_rows`. Its seven measurement
columns are `counts`, `fpkm`, `tpm`, `log2_fc`, `p_value`, `z_score` and
`other_value`. Preserve their native values, including fractional counts,
negative values and measured zero, with source locations, units, denominator
meaning, origin and uncertainty where available. A reported p-value does not
establish its correction method; absent replication and units remain unknown.
Do not derive a coordinate-based coverage without a verified coordinate
convention. Preserve `genome_feature` one-based inclusive endpoints and strand.

These deterministic functions operate on supplied data without network calls,
jobs, LLM judgments or resource changes. Saved sheets permit recalculation
without reacquisition. Counts, sequence-join totals and successful retrieval
are not annotation-confidence scores. Native vocabulary and reference records
may legitimately contain no scientific numerical measurement. Tool information,
internal sheets and calculators are separate from evidence-axis grading and
W05 annotation-credit aggregation.

Keep `not_selected`, absent, native null, not measured, invalid, unrepresentable,
truncated, failed and measured zero distinct. Requesting a registered field that
was not acquired returns `not_selected`. Native arrays containing unsupported
nested values retain their complete raw bytes and an invalid scalar projection;
they are not flattened or replaced with fabricated nulls. Preserve other valid
cells and rows. A failed parse has null counts and an explicit unavailable
reason; it is not an empty successful page. A failed facet has no bucket, while
a native missing-field bucket retains its actual bucket identity and count.

## Retained artifacts and typed return

The publisher retains the exact complete native response as the source's raw
artifact and the complete `PublishedGrading` as a linked grading artifact. The
grading contains the prepared request, original selector, parse result,
page/facet components, selected join sheets/components and explicit input
bindings. A compact projection never replaces the retained native response.

The publication outcome has `status`, `operation_ref`, `record_refs`,
`changed_record_refs`, `result` and `feedback`. Its `result` fields are
`source_ref`, `raw_artifact_ref`, `grading_artifact_ref`, `collection`, `mode`,
`parse_status`, `qualification`, `requested_projection_complete` and
`projection_failures`. The execution host adds its actual acquisition receipt
and original handoff reference. Publication returns one source for the
acquisition; rows and buckets do not become separately scored source records.

After host custody and receiver-possession qualification,
`bvbrc_data_views.project_bvbrc_data_facts` supplies only the requested closed
parent-form facts:

| Fact source | Available meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `execution_bvbrc_pages` | Requested row window, actual nullable row counts, total/exactness, completeness, coverage, continuation and unavailable reason. |
| `execution_bvbrc_counts` | Native matching-document count, exact query population and availability; no fabricated count after failure. |
| `execution_bvbrc_facets` | Selected native field buckets, count, same-population denominator/fraction and bucket-window qualifications; facet mode only. |
| `execution_bvbrc_numeric_rows` | Selected row indices, native identifiers, numerical values, unit/denominator/origin/uncertainty relationships, selected metadata cells and explicit unavailable fields. |
| `execution_bvbrc_feature_sequence_rows` | Selected feature occurrences, AA/NA sequence joins, optional sequence values, lengths, hash/length agreement and join qualifications. |
| `execution_bvbrc_expression_rows` | Selected molecular measurements and their result/bioset/experiment/feature relationships, source-level metadata and unavailable fields. |

Native text, including product names and conditions, is source data. Its values
never supply episode instructions. Typed cell references identify exact retained
values and their relationships; host materialization supplies admitted values
without a new lookup action or a model-composed restatement. This library entry
does not define or modify recurring TASK/STEERING rendering.

HTTP errors preserve actual status, body and relevant headers. Incomplete
transport, incompatible profile, malformed JSON, invalid selected values and
join conflicts retain specific failure records and useful partial data. A
source record alone does not establish completion of the requested result.
Validated practical completion uses the existing controller and exact-zero
future expectation; it does not declare the scientific annotation complete.

the actual endpoint and any authorization configuration; an available operation

and the parent's fixed selector. Its action arguments are `{}`. Legacy selector

pair metadata. The explicit selector also supports these choices:

| Selected mode | Required input | Work performed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `native_result` | Original handoff; `saved_result_ref` is null | Parse the retained response and calculate components using the selected `pair_metadata`. |
| `saved_sheet` | Original handoff and a previously received MinHash `saved_result_ref` for that same request and response | Reuse that saved sheet and calculate components using the selected `pair_metadata`. |

Neither choice repeats the search or acquires metadata. A saved-sheet
recalculation is a new selected calculation of retained data, not a fresh native
acquisition. Replaying an already completed selected action returns its original
saved output. Earlier publications and returns retain their original values.

row order, duplicate genome rows, strings/numbers and malformed fields in the
retained output. The same numerical sheet keeps parsed quantities beside those

recalculated distance and p-value.

`genome_id`, and supplies all four fields `kmer_length`, `query_length`,
`reference_length` and `alphabet_size`. Each field is a positive integer or null
when unavailable. k-mer length counts sequence symbols per k-mer; query and
reference lengths are the explicitly supplied length operands; alphabet size is
the declared cardinality used by the calculation. It is not the number of
different letters observed in a sequence. An empty `pair_metadata` list supplies
no parameters. Numeric strings, booleans and assumed defaults are not inputs.

evidence item naming that `field`, its `source_ref`, the source's retained
`artifact_ref`, and the RFC 6901 JSON pointer `record_path` to the same integer.

return or the parent's selected inputs. A null field has no evidence item. The
selected artifact must belong to that source as its original native or bound
auxiliary artifact. A stored source alone is insufficient. Preserve every selected
metadata record; do not merge duplicate genome occurrences or silently choose
between two records for the same pair. The calculator joins by both row index
and genome ID and retains mismatch or ambiguity diagnostics.

alphabet size or reference release. Current genome metadata, supplied sequence
lengths, upstream defaults or numerical agreement do not establish which
parameters the remote sketch used. Keep `native_parameter_equivalence` equal to
`unestablished` for supplied calculations.

for an identified row with valid counts and a positive denominator. It describes
the sampled hash union, not bases, genome coverage or the search population.

p-value also requires both lengths and alphabet size. `unsaturated_distance`
preserves the distance before the calculator's cap, where available. The
recalculated p-value is the existing binomial upper-tail calculation under the
explicit supplied model inputs. Missing inputs leave only the dependent
components null. A zero union leaves derived values null. Preserve saved
precision, saturation and numerical-range diagnostics. Native parse status and
calculation availability are separate.

| --- | --- |

| `bvbrc_minhash_calculations` | Saved calculated components, the four saved pair input fields, unestablished native-parameter equivalence and row diagnostic codes. |

Only requested typed facts cross the child return. Source-only or counts-only
returns do not supply match or calculation facts. The complete response, sheet,
inputs and diagnostics remain retained. Usable partial measurements survive
missing or invalid neighbors; unavailable values are not zero. Empty results do
not establish a complete negative search. These measurements are dimensionless
except for the explicit integer counts and length operands, and none is a
calibrated probability of gene function.

# Retrieve the assigned BV-BRC genome, feature or protein-family data

Run the public BV-BRC data query the parent assigned and return the source data
it requested. Preserve its collection, filters, selected fields, ordering and
page. Use the returned subjects and native values to identify what was actually
retrieved; a database's functional label does not establish the target gene's
measured activity.

The configured service is `bvbrc_data`. Its default Data API location is
`https://www.bv-brc.org/api`. A caller can explicitly configure another BV-BRC
deployment's base URL and request timeout. The query does not accept a URL,
credentials or arbitrary HTTP method. Public data was retrieved without an
authorization token during verification on 2026-10-23. That observation does not
guarantee future service availability.

## Specify the actual query

The request contains:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `collection` | `genome`, `genome_feature` or `protein_family_ref`. |
| `filters` | An array of field/operator/value predicates. They are combined with AND. An empty array requests the selected collection's first assigned page. |
| Filter `field` | The actual BV-BRC field name, such as `gene`, `feature_id`, `genome_id`, `accession`, `pgfam_id`, `plfam_id` or `family_id`, as appropriate to the collection. |
| Filter `operator` | `eq`, `ne`, `gt`, `lt` or `in`. `in` requires a nonempty array of scalar values; the other operators require a scalar. |
| Filter `value` | A literal string, number or boolean, or an array for `in`. Values are encoded individually; text inside a value cannot add another RQL operation. |
| `fields` | Optional array of returned field names. If omitted or empty, the service's default fields are returned. Unknown or absent returned fields are not filled with invented values. |
| `sort` | Optional array of `{field, direction}` objects, where direction is `asc` or `desc`. Choose relevant stable ordering when comparing pages. |
| `limit` | Positive number of records requested on this page; default 25. This is a page-size operand, not an investigation quota. |
| `offset` | Nonnegative starting result offset; default zero. |

The original assignment keeps any omitted optional fields omitted. Defaults are
resolved only into the selected native request. The client sends one GET using
the documented RQL expressions, including `limit(count,start)`. It does not
retrieve subsequent pages automatically.

For example, locating reference records named ybhP can use collection
`genome_feature` and filter `{field: gene, operator: eq, value: ybhP}`. Such a
query can return proteins from many genomes. Retain each actual `feature_id`,
`genome_id`, organism label and replicon accession rather than treating every
row as the fixed gene under annotation.

To examine a particular genome's neighbors, use explicit genome and replicon
filters together with the selected coordinate interval. Preserve the source's
one-based inclusive `start` and `end` and separate `strand`. The client neither
converts them to target coordinates nor infers neighborhood membership,
homology, co-expression or functional association scores. For family queries,
keep PGF/PLF membership and family descriptions as the source's reported data.

## Choose an available operation

`api.bvbrc.query` takes empty arguments and retrieves the original assigned
query's one page. A successful response is already completed data retrieval.
There is no remote job identifier, queue or running state to manufacture, and
no status-poll operation for this service. Validated response metadata can
establish the requested usable handoff. The original practical endpoint and
configured controller determine closure; retrieving a page does not complete
the scientific annotation.

`api.bvbrc.result` takes empty arguments in the results episode. Its parent's
selector may contain only `offset` and `limit`; the original collection, filters,
fields and ordering remain fixed. An empty selector retains the original page.
When the selected effective page matches the original page, acquire the actual
retained response without another HTTP request. A different selected offset or
limit makes exactly one new data request. Changing the scientific query requires
an explicitly assigned request, rather than an unrecorded substitution.

## Read the actual page and preserve its limits

The JSON response is an array of native source rows. Result publication retains
the exact response bytes and request/response provenance and returns the rows
with page metadata. It creates no target assay, assessment or annotation. A
missing family, protein accession or condition field stays missing; it is not
evidence that the biological feature is absent. Zero returned rows is a
completed empty query result, not proof against a gene function.

Keep `Content-Range` verbatim. An observed response with two rows reported
`items 0-2/88287`; that end value must not be treated as an inclusive last row.
The next offset uses the requested offset plus the actual returned row count.
The total is reported only when the native header supplies it. A missing total
remains unknown. A continuation identifies another possible page; it does not
select another action or prove the query should continue.

Use observation times when comparing service facts. A monitor can report the
retained immediate response's terminal observation; there is no new remote job
to poll. Keep HTTP response time distinct from queue, execution and total
turnaround measurements. This provider does not invent those unmeasured
intervals or a duration forecast.

Failures preserve the actual response when one was received. HTTP errors retain
status, body and relevant headers such as `Retry-After`. A redirect is recorded
without following it. An incomplete body retains its partial bytes and cannot
establish a completed handoff. Requests are not retried automatically. Preserve
specific failure information and useful partial results so the responsible
episode can choose its next action.

## Distinguish public data from BV-BRC computational jobs

BV-BRC also has an authenticated computational AppService, separate from this
public Data API. The official AppService client uses
`https://p3.theseed.org/services/app_service`; BV-BRC's architecture documentation
also lists `https://www.bv-brc.org/services/app_service`. An unauthenticated
read-only request to the former returned the explicit JSON-RPC error
"Authentication required for AppService but no authentication header was
passed" during verification. The latter returned a Cloudflare HTML rejection;
that proxy response is different from an application authentication result.

AppService submission, monitoring and Workspace result operations are not
implemented or exposed by this `bvbrc_data` provider. Documentation about
`start_app` does not make it an available operation. Do not represent a public
data page as a submitted computational job or claim that authenticated BV-BRC
computations were tested.

## Primary sources

- BV-BRC Data API: https://www.bv-brc.org/api/doc/
- Genome features and field meanings: https://www.bv-brc.org/api/doc/genome_feature
- Protein-family references: https://www.bv-brc.org/api/doc/protein_family_ref
- Official Data API implementation and RQL protocol: https://github.com/BV-BRC/BV-BRC-API/blob/master/README.md
- BV-BRC service architecture: https://www.bv-brc.org/docs/system_documentation/system_architecture.html
- AppService specification: https://github.com/BV-BRC/app_service/blob/master/AppService.spec
- Official AppService client: https://github.com/BV-BRC/BV-BRC-Go-SDK/blob/main/appservice/client.go

`https://www.bv-brc.org/api`. A caller can explicitly configure another BV-BRC
deployment's base URL and request timeout. The query does not accept a URL,
credentials or arbitrary HTTP method. Public data was retrieved without an
authorization token during verification on 2026-10-23. That observation does not
guarantee future service availability.

## Specify the actual query

The request contains:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `collection` | `genome`, `genome_feature` or `protein_family_ref`. |
| `filters` | An array of field/operator/value predicates. They are combined with AND. An empty array requests the selected collection's first assigned page. |
| Filter `field` | The actual BV-BRC field name, such as `gene`, `feature_id`, `genome_id`, `accession`, `pgfam_id`, `plfam_id` or `family_id`, as appropriate to the collection. |
| Filter `operator` | `eq`, `ne`, `gt`, `lt` or `in`. `in` requires a nonempty array of scalar values; the other operators require a scalar. |
| Filter `value` | A literal string, number or boolean, or an array for `in`. Values are encoded individually; text inside a value cannot add another RQL operation. |
| `fields` | Optional array of returned field names. If omitted or empty, the service's default fields are returned. Unknown or absent returned fields are not filled with invented values. |
| `sort` | Optional array of `{field, direction}` objects, where direction is `asc` or `desc`. Choose relevant stable ordering when comparing pages. |
| `limit` | Positive number of records requested on this page; default 25. This is a page-size operand, not an investigation quota. |
| `offset` | Nonnegative starting result offset; default zero. |

The original assignment keeps any omitted optional fields omitted. Defaults are
resolved only into the selected native request. The client sends one GET using
the documented RQL expressions, including `limit(count,start)`. It does not
retrieve subsequent pages automatically.

For example, locating reference records named ybhP can use collection
`genome_feature` and filter `{field: gene, operator: eq, value: ybhP}`. Such a
query can return proteins from many genomes. Retain each actual `feature_id`,
`genome_id`, organism label and replicon accession rather than treating every
row as the fixed gene under annotation.

To examine a particular genome's neighbors, use explicit genome and replicon
filters together with the selected coordinate interval. Preserve the source's
one-based inclusive `start` and `end` and separate `strand`. The client neither
converts them to target coordinates nor infers neighborhood membership,
homology, co-expression or functional association scores. For family queries,
keep PGF/PLF membership and family descriptions as the source's reported data.

## Choose an available operation

`api.bvbrc.query` takes empty arguments and retrieves the original assigned
query's one page. A successful response is already completed data retrieval.
There is no remote job identifier, queue or running state to manufacture, and
no status-poll operation for this service. Validated response metadata can
establish the requested usable handoff. The original practical endpoint and
configured controller determine closure; retrieving a page does not complete
the scientific annotation.

`api.bvbrc.result` takes empty arguments in the results episode. Its parent's
selector may contain only `offset` and `limit`; the original collection, filters,
fields and ordering remain fixed. An empty selector retains the original page.
When the selected effective page matches the original page, acquire the actual
retained response without another HTTP request. A different selected offset or
limit makes exactly one new data request. Changing the scientific query requires
an explicitly assigned request, rather than an unrecorded substitution.

## Read the actual page and preserve its limits

The JSON response is an array of native source rows. Result publication retains
the exact response bytes and request/response provenance and returns the rows
with page metadata. It creates no target assay, assessment or annotation. A
missing family, protein accession or condition field stays missing; it is not
evidence that the biological feature is absent. Zero returned rows is a
completed empty query result, not proof against a gene function.

Keep `Content-Range` verbatim. An observed response with two rows reported
`items 0-2/88287`; that end value must not be treated as an inclusive last row.
The next offset uses the requested offset plus the actual returned row count.
The total is reported only when the native header supplies it. A missing total
remains unknown. A continuation identifies another possible page; it does not
select another action or prove the query should continue.

Use observation times when comparing service facts. A monitor can report the
retained immediate response's terminal observation; there is no new remote job
to poll. Keep HTTP response time distinct from queue, execution and total
turnaround measurements. This provider does not invent those unmeasured
intervals or a duration forecast.

Failures preserve the actual response when one was received. HTTP errors retain
status, body and relevant headers such as `Retry-After`. A redirect is recorded
without following it. An incomplete body retains its partial bytes and cannot
establish a completed handoff. Requests are not retried automatically. Preserve
specific failure information and useful partial results so the responsible
episode can choose its next action.

## Distinguish public data from BV-BRC computational jobs

BV-BRC also has an authenticated computational AppService, separate from this
public Data API. The official AppService client uses
`https://p3.theseed.org/services/app_service`; BV-BRC's architecture documentation
also lists `https://www.bv-brc.org/services/app_service`. An unauthenticated
read-only request to the former returned the explicit JSON-RPC error
"Authentication required for AppService but no authentication header was
passed" during verification. The latter returned a Cloudflare HTML rejection;
that proxy response is different from an application authentication result.

AppService submission, monitoring and Workspace result operations are not
implemented or exposed by this `bvbrc_data` provider. Documentation about
`start_app` does not make it an available operation. Do not represent a public
data page as a submitted computational job or claim that authenticated BV-BRC
computations were tested.

## Primary sources

- BV-BRC Data API: https://www.bv-brc.org/api/doc/
- Genome features and field meanings: https://www.bv-brc.org/api/doc/genome_feature
- Protein-family references: https://www.bv-brc.org/api/doc/protein_family_ref
- Official Data API implementation and RQL protocol: https://github.com/BV-BRC/BV-BRC-API/blob/master/README.md
- BV-BRC service architecture: https://www.bv-brc.org/docs/system_documentation/system_architecture.html
- AppService specification: https://github.com/BV-BRC/app_service/blob/master/AppService.spec
- Official AppService client: https://github.com/BV-BRC/BV-BRC-Go-SDK/blob/main/appservice/client.go

Use the caller-bound API client or the actual assigned API-execution episode. Use the registered operation contract, configured service/contact and actual request or job identity. A service operation requiring an execution assignment is available only in that assigned resource episode; this information does not make it an ordinary ToolRegistry operation. # HMMER API result measurements

Acquire the originally requested phmmer or hmmscan result page through
`api.hmmer.result`. The result assignment fixes the original search and selected
page; this operation takes no new query, database or threshold. Another page
requires another explicit results assignment. The service's complete raw page
is retained, including all supplied hit identifiers, linked metadata, domain
arrays, alignment displays, reporting/inclusion flags and search statistics.

For phmmer, model coordinates describe the query and sequence coordinates
describe a matched reference protein. For hmmscan, model coordinates describe
the profile and sequence coordinates describe the query protein. A profile's
consensus is not a measured reference protein. Coordinates are retained in their
native one-based inclusive form and interpreted through zero-based half-open
intervals. Query length must agree with the actual submitted sequence.

The tool preserves separate full-sequence and domain scores, conditional and
independent E-values, bias, alignment spans, envelopes, paired positions,
insertions/deletions and coverage denominators. A domain's span coverage uses
the span and the full corresponding model/sequence length. Paired coverage uses
only columns containing both a model position and a sequence residue. These can
differ in a gapped alignment. Missing alignment displays or operand metadata
leave their dependent measurements unavailable; native scores can remain useful.

Identity quantities have different meanings. `api_identity_fraction` retains
the provider's identity count divided by the smaller ungapped display length.
`consensus_identity_fraction` uses matching consensus/residue columns divided by
paired columns; `alignment_identity_fraction` uses all alignment columns.
`sequence_identity_fraction` is available only when supplied actual sequence
operands establish that correspondence. None is a probability of correct gene
function. A profile-consensus match must not be described as sequence identity.

Native domain bias is supplied in nats by this API; its separately named bits
value divides by ln(2). Local native tables already report bias in bits.
`native_accuracy` and the PP display concern alignment posterior accuracy, not
identity or gene-function confidence. PP symbols supply probability intervals;
the reported lower/upper means retain those bounds instead of inventing an
exact probability. Printed zero E-values remain zero with their native meaning.

The numerical sheet and calculators retain the original hit-array and
domain-array positions. These are distinct from provider hit indices or native
domain ordinals. Invalid domains preserve valid siblings and raw bytes with
specific failure information. Repeated accessions, overlapping domains or
multiple representations do not establish independent evidence. Linked UniProt
metadata and the actual native target name remain separate identities.

A completed page does not establish a complete hit population. Pagination and
native search statistics remain explicit, and a no-hit page does not establish
biological absence. These measurements do not assign a function or lineage.
Full sheets and alignments remain retained data; the parent receives its
requested typed facts. Grading makes no additional service requests, model
calls or completed actions. Search timing remains separate from these
scientific measurements.

# API results, failures and timing

The `results` episode receives `execution_results_assignment_v1` with the
original `handoff_ref` and `selector` containing positive `page` and optional
`page_size`. Its `api.hmmer.result` action takes empty arguments: it cannot
change the job or substitute a different requested page. Another page can be
requested through another explicitly commissioned results assignment.

A successful result must contain a usable non-null result object and agree
with the saved UUID, algorithm, database and input identity where reported.
The implementation retains raw response bytes, request/transport provenance,
pagination, native statistics, accessions, scores, E-values and domain
coordinates. Valid partial publication survives a later failure. Malformed
responses, identity conflicts, not-ready results, provider failure and uncertain
submission remain distinct outcomes available for repair.

A completed page is not every page. `hmmscan` hits are profiles/families;
`phmmer` hits are reference proteins. Acquisition does not assign function or
lineage, and a no-hit page does not establish biological absence. The scientific
parent receives typed references and interprets the actual retained records.

Replay returns the original saved outcome without another HTTP request. Repeated
information does not manufacture credit. Complete acquisition of the requested
page establishes the results endpoint and immediately gives exact zero future
expected credit, preserving the final actual gain.

Provider-reported search time, HTTP time, queue wait and total turnaround are
different quantities. Use only measured intervals and keep unknowns unknown.
Monitoring records are separate from closed launch receipts and histories.
Instruction retrieval itself is neither a timing sample nor scientific evidence.

The historical service schema and database observations are documented in
source rows S2–S6 of the launch instruction source record. They do not establish
present service availability. Wiring verification uses controlled HTTP responses;
it does not establish a live configured-model API run.

The `results` episode receives `execution_results_assignment_v1` with the
original `handoff_ref` and `selector` containing positive `page` and optional
`page_size`. Its `api.hmmer.result` action takes empty arguments: it cannot
change the job or substitute a different requested page. Another page can be
requested through another explicitly commissioned results assignment.

A successful result must contain a usable non-null result object and agree
with the saved UUID, algorithm, database and input identity where reported.
The implementation retains raw response bytes, request/transport provenance,
pagination, native statistics, accessions, scores, E-values and domain
coordinates. Valid partial publication survives a later failure. Malformed
responses, identity conflicts, not-ready results, provider failure and uncertain
submission remain distinct outcomes available for repair.

A completed page is not every page. `hmmscan` hits are profiles/families;
`phmmer` hits are reference proteins. Acquisition does not assign function or
lineage, and a no-hit page does not establish biological absence. The scientific
parent receives typed references and interprets the actual retained records.

Replay returns the original saved outcome without another HTTP request. Repeated
information does not manufacture credit. Complete acquisition of the requested
page establishes the results endpoint and immediately gives exact zero future
expected credit, preserving the final actual gain.

Provider-reported search time, HTTP time, queue wait and total turnaround are
different quantities. Use only measured intervals and keep unknowns unknown.
Monitoring records are separate from closed launch receipts and histories.
Instruction retrieval itself is neither a timing sample nor scientific evidence.

source rows S2–S6 of the launch instruction source record. They do not establish
present service availability. Wiring verification uses controlled HTTP responses;
it does not establish a live configured-model API run.

# Retrieve the assigned protein information from UniProt

Use the assigned accession or search query to obtain UniProt records needed for
the parent's investigation. Preserve the original query, scientific scope and
requested result. Decide which available request or retained response supplies
that result; neither a paper's citation nor a functional label replaces the
actual record. UniProt entries describe their source proteins. They do not
establish an experiment on the annotation target.

## Assigned request and available operations

This API resource uses service `uniprot` in `api_service_assignment_v1`. Its
closed request is either `{operation: "record", accession: "..."}` or
`{operation: "search", query: "...", size?: integer, cursor?: "..."}`. Search
size is 1–500; an omitted size is resolved to 10 in the actual command without
rewriting the parent's original request. Use only explicitly supplied accessions,
queries and constraints. Credentials are not required for these public reads.

| Operation | Available work |
| --- | --- |
| `api.uniprot.record` | In API execution, one record request for the assigned accession. |
| `api.uniprot.search` | In API execution, one page for the original query and any assigned cursor. |
| `api.uniprot.collect` | In results acquisition, publish the retained original response, or request the specifically selected cursor page. |

Each operation takes empty arguments; the original assignment and requested
result selector supply the meaningful inputs. No operation traverses pages,
polls, retries, changes the annotation target or interprets function in a private
loop. Use preparation and earlier outcomes to decide what useful work remains.

The public endpoints are `GET https://rest.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/{accession}`
and `GET https://rest.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/search` with the query, size, JSON
format and any selected cursor. A search returns one page; the response's
`Link` header supplies its actual next cursor when another page is available.
Retain that cursor and any reported total count/release information. Do not
construct a cursor from page numbers or treat a page as the entire result set.

## Reuse, publication and completion

A successful immediate response completes the assigned record/page request;
there is no remote job to invent or monitor. Its validated handoff retains the
actual response for the results episode. Empty result selector `{}` consumes
that retained response without another HTTP request. For a search, selector
`{cursor?: "...", size?: integer}` requests one explicitly selected page of the
same original query. A record result requires an empty selector. A changed
selector is different requested work, not permission to alter the query.

Publication retains original response bytes, request/transport provenance,
source subjects, sequences, source annotations and returned pagination. Inspect
the actual protein and organism behind a record before transferring a conclusion
to the target. Preserve conflicting source labels and missing evidence as such.
An empty search page describes that query and page; it is not proof that the
gene lacks a function. A failed request is an access failure.

Replay and cached publication reuse the same actual response. Repeated source
content does not create an additional contribution. Validated completion of the
original practical request sets its future expected credit to zero while
retaining the final actual gain. Completing one requested page does not complete
an unrestricted biological investigation. Keep HTTP time, scientific support
and the episode's own yields distinct.

tool_info.description: Compare explicitly corresponding protein CA coordinates using a proper unweighted rigid fit or a supplied moving-to-fixed transform, with separately selected evaluation sites.
tool_info.instructions: Supply operation=compare with fixed_selection and moving_selection, one model and chain on each side, explicit correspondence, calculation parameters and selected metadata files. Correspondence is an injective collinear explicit residue map or an explicitly selected retained Biopython protein local/global alignment with full native traceback, original grading artifact and both authenticated extraction sequence/map descriptors. The existing scientific-child sequence.align uses BLOSUM62, gap open -10 and gap extension -0.5; obtain that result separately when needed. This comparison performs no alignment, chain search, outlier removal or conformer search. In fit_then_evaluate_ca, declare fit_selection separately from evaluation_selection; only selected fit CA pairs determine the unweighted proper rigid transform. In evaluate_declared_transform_ca, provide the exact proper rotation and translation and no fit selection. The convention is row-vector y@R+t, moving to fixed, in angstroms. Native protein_structure_native_v1 retains the complete numerical sheet and baseline: original coordinates, exact correspondence, CA availability, denominators, fit diagnostics, transform and requested site measurements. Declare require_all or use_available for missing coordinates, numerical tolerances, optional descriptive distance threshold and explicit coordinate-output sets. Degenerate fits retain a computable minimum but do not invent a unique transform. B factors, native pLDDT, PAE and reported uncertainties retain their actual semantics and units; they are not fit weights or annotation probabilities. Saved-sheet recalculation uses a separate deterministic calculator with explicit new parameters and preserves the original baseline. Declare the selected Software interpreter, version, dependency versions and implementation hashes, exact input artifacts, SHA-256/byte lengths and absolute authorized staging paths. The closed requested_job contains the compiled worker argv, explicit environment and native_protein_structure job. Output paths are fixed: result.json, stdout.log, stderr.log, with the extraction outputs described above. Commission launch and its configured launch_local child with 20 GiB RAM, 4 GiB scratch, zero swap and no wall-time budget. Preparation only reserves the attempt; the owning child selects practical.job.start. Status reads the original durable identity and available logs; a retry requires a separately selected failed-attempt retry. The sealed bundle retains the original plan, worker input, complete declared files and structured failures. Native execution success, complete capture and delivery of the parent's requested typed results remain separate. Resource choice and further investigation belong to the episode. This entry provides no API or HPC deployment and grants no direct execution operation to the root.

# Gene prediction with Pyrodigal

`genes.predict` runs Pyrodigal on the supplied sequence or selected interval.
Select `meta` or `single` and the genetic code explicitly. These are distinct
prediction models; the operation does not substitute one after a failed run.
The existing local execution binding enforces the caller's memory and scratch
limits. A short input can be unsuitable for single-genome model training;
preserve that failure rather than inventing candidates or changing mode.

Each candidate retains its interval, strand, partial-boundary flags,
translation, native model score and native confidence percentage. The
confidence describes the native gene prediction, not the correctness of a
functional annotation. Predictions remain candidates.

The numerical sheet keeps both the worker's zero-based, half-open coordinates
within the submitted region and their coordinates in the original sequence.
It measures candidate nucleotide length, protein length excluding stop
symbols, internal stops and terminal stops. The region's coding coverage is
the union of valid candidate intervals divided by the submitted nucleotide
length, so overlaps and repeated intervals do not multiply coverage. Missing
or invalid candidate fields remain explicit; coverage from only the valid
subset is marked incomplete. An empty successful prediction differs from a
failed prediction.

Preserve the complete native candidate list and populated numerical sheet.
Return the parent's requested candidate measurements and coordinate mappings.
Native score values and derived measurements remain separate; no function
confidence or annotation-credit formula is assigned by this tool.

Extract a selected page of actual native measurements; explicit snapshot for later pages and retry_from for an explicit failed-attempt retry. Parent integrates scientific meaning.

Use the actual local binding and its caller-owned resource limits. Read or measure only the assigned operands and explicit received inputs. Reuse retained outputs when the operation is a read; do not treat a read as a new measurement. Preserve native values, coordinate meanings, partial results and actionable failures. Job-specific operations require their original assigned execution.

Use exactly the separately supplied actual input_schema; required operands and allowed values come from that contract. Do not infer another callable, resource or environment from this entry.

The native outputs are native.stdout, native.stderr, hits.tbl and domains.tbl. The caller's result adapter binds them to the original query, reference database and execution identity. A search match is evidence, not an assigned annotation, orthology assertion or substrate-specific assay.

homology.extract acquires a selected page with an explicit limit. Use its returned snapshot_ref for subsequent pages of the same captured results. homology.coverage reads recorded parsed/acquired row coverage and parser/native completion; it does not poll the job or parse it again. homology.errors reads typed extraction failures from that snapshot. An explicit retry_from identifies a failed extraction attempt; inspect what needs changing before retrying.

The requested result references return through the parent's form. The scientific parent integrates them. Successful native termination, extraction completion and episode yielding do not establish that a biological question is resolved. Preserve valid acquired rows when another component fails.

# Existing detached phmmer local binding

Use this section when the caller binds the existing `ResourceEpisodes` local
homology resource or the original `HomologyEpisodes` job roles. That local
launch exposes `homology.*` tools. The other local sections describe the
separate opt-in practical binding's `practical.*` operations. These bindings
have distinct assignment formats and are not assembled or interchangeable
merely because this library documents both. Only the actual episode catalog
determines which operations can be selected.

The parent supplies an in-scope protein `query_ref`, CPU allocation and an
enabled search mode; the caller's registry fixes executable/database paths and
digests, maximum CPU and local limits. Ordering freezes the normalized query
FASTA, CPU and mode under the original operation/job identity. `native_defaults`
uses native heuristic filters; `maximum_sensitivity` adds `--max` only when
enabled and selected. It can cost more time and does not establish a function
or stronger significance. No timing transfer between modes is assumed.
An `existing_job_ref` repairs the same immutable job rather than changing its
query, CPU, mode, inputs or native reservation. Resource assignments additionally
retain exact resource selection, caller allocation and supplied input pins.

| Actual operation | Owning role and behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `homology.environment` | `launch_local` / original `job_launch`: inspect configured file presence, assigned CPU/mode, staging, intent and limits. |
| `homology.configure` | Same launch roles: check/apply the assigned CPU and pinned executable; empty arguments do not select a different CPU. |
| `homology.stage` | Same launch roles: prepare/repair private query/reference snapshots and reuse unchanged inputs; preserve the original database. |
| `homology.submit` | Same launch roles: validate pinned dependencies and submit the registered detached job once. Replay retains the original identity. |

| `homology.check_handoff` | Same launch roles: open a fresh persistent receiver and check exact job/registry/interfaces, status, elapsed time and output availability. |
| `homology.sample` | Original `job_monitor`, not local launch: retain an actual selected status sample for an admitted handoff. |
| `homology.extract` | Resource `results` / original `job_results`: acquire a selected native-result page with explicit `limit`; use its `snapshot_ref` for later pages and explicit `retry_from` for a failed extraction attempt. |

uncertain submission does not authorize another physical search. A usable
handoff is an operational receiving-interface result, not scientific completion.

tool_info.instructions:
Operation: image.view

Inspect one explicitly selected frame of a registered scientific image. The next reasoning call receives its actual pixels and exact source/frame metadata. Stored axes are preserved; no contrast adjustment, resizing, interpretation or annotation is performed. An optional RGB conversion is explicit and recorded; original bytes remain intact.

Use the actual local binding and its caller-owned resource limits. Read or measure only the assigned operands and explicit received inputs. Use exactly the separately supplied actual input_schema; required operands and allowed values come from that contract. Do not infer another callable, resource or environment from this entry.

source.read takes a source_ref and a selected representation. It returns an exact artifact and UTF-8 byte range suitable for a textual scientific anchor. Preserve the actual quote and coordinate frame. Original XML and its paragraph projection are different representations; an offset in one cannot be used for the other.

For a PDF, source.pdf.info exposes physical page information. source.pdf.text extracts one chosen physical page using the selected reading_order, layout or raw mode. Extracted text is a derived source with its own UTF-8 byte coordinates; these are not original PDF byte positions. The current local parser uses Poppler. This entry does not claim PyMuPDF or OCR is installed.

source.pdf.page renders a selected physical page into a retained image. image.view explicitly supplies a selected frame's pixels to the next reasoning call. Rendering alone does not deliver those pixels or interpret a figure. A visual observation uses its actual image view and pixel region; it is not a literal text extraction or a performed experiment.

Different representations can expose different useful information. The episode can inspect outcomes, change approach, or delegate a substantive iterative reading question. A one-off page extraction remains a tool call. No fixed parse strategy, full-document reading requirement or coverage threshold is imposed by these instructions.

# Actual practical HPC operations

These operations exist in the opt-in practical HPC binding. Their presence in
this library does not make them available in a different binding. The caller
must supply a real `pbs_ssh` configuration: `workspace`, `ssh_argv`,
`python_executable` and `account`. No transport, credentials, queue or software
is discovered or selected automatically by that configuration.

| Callable operation | Actual selected work |
| --- | --- |
| `practical.inspect` | Observe the original assignment's declared path predicates. |
| `practical.inventory.refresh` | Read a selected structured catalog within the workspace and reconcile the local mirror. |
| `practical.context.set` | Persist a validated cwd and explicit environment for later actions. |
| `practical.directory.create` | Create a selected project directory. |
| `practical.file.write` | Write the exact selected UTF-8 text in project storage. |
| `practical.file.read` | Read a selected byte window, retaining original bytes and offsets. |
| `practical.command.run` | Run one selected preparation or diagnostic command on the configured remote host, retaining its outcome and logs. |
| `practical.job.start` | Submit the fixed requested job with selected `queue` and `resources`; the caller owns the account. |
| `practical.job.status` | Observe the original PBS execution, exposed scheduler fields and log tails. |
| `practical.job.collect` | Observe that execution and validate the assignment's requested output predicates. |

`cd`/`export` within a command affects that subprocess only. Use the context
operation for persistent changes. The requested job's explicit environment is
not replaced with a preparation command's environment. The worker applies
project-confined temporary/cache defaults and records native submission state.

The original attempt is identified by a saved intent, submission token and,
when known, the actual PBS ID. Reopening reconciles that identity; an interrupted
or failed SSH/qsub reply does not establish scheduler rejection. Unknown work
is not resubmitted. An explicit `retry_failed_execution_id` may start a new
attempt only for that confirmed failed original execution. No retry is made
automatically, and retry without an actual PBS ID is unsupported.

Status/collection can receive `receipt_ref` from a scoped prior practical
handoff. They check the original job/resource identity and record the receiving
episode's observation. Native completion and declared output predicates, not a
prose claim, establish the endpoint. Existing output alone need not establish
that this job produced it; use the assignment's exact hash predicates where
required. Log tails are bounded; select a further file window when useful.

The new practical PBS path has fixture verification, not a live ALCF run.

wire PBS observations through the general recursive MonitorEpisodes interface.

# Local assignment, setup and reuse

The parent supplies the requested job, workspace, constraints, validated
endpoint and typed return form. The child chooses useful preparation, reuse,
diagnosis and execution actions within that assignment. These instructions are
supporting information; they are not a fixed action order or a complete episode.

The opt-in local practical binding requires an explicit configuration with
`kind=local`, an absolute `workspace` and a caller-owned resource `policy`.
The project's goal retains 20 GiB RAM, 4 GiB scratch and no wall-time budget.
Use the actual caller policy and preserve assignment constraints; instructions
cannot grant a larger allocation or silently add a timeout.

The supplied inventory snapshot describes known preparations before the first
choice. Its canonical content hash and local/remote comparison identify catalog
bytes, not present runtime usability. Decide from the assigned software and
input requirements whether an existing executable, environment, database or
prepared wrapper needs checking. Reuse a valid setup. If something is missing
or incompatible, choose a scoped preparation/repair action and retain its
actual result. Do not silently substitute another database or algorithm.

Record executable/source/package and database identities at the specificity the
job needs. A file existing at an old path is weaker than a checked release/hash
or a successful relevant operation. Changes in load/free space/throughput are
current observations, separate from the reusable setup. Repairing one run's
conditions does not require rebuilding that setup or rewriting old records.

Native execution requires `systemd-run`, `systemctl`, a usable user systemd
manager and verified cgroup limits. Failure to establish that boundary returns
an operational failure; no unprotected fallback is installed. The native
lifecycle controls the process tree independently of the episode. Memory and
swap have cgroup limits; scratch is monitored with possible overshoot and a
per-file limit. This does not constitute a filesystem sandbox. Keep selected
files and generated control/output paths in the supplied workspace. Source
rows L1–L3 in `docs/LAUNCH_INSTRUCTION_SOURCES_2026-10-22_001.md`.

# Local handles, results and failures

The original requested job has a durable disk handle and systemd execution
identity. Recovery observes that handle; it does not repeat submission because
the episode or caller restarted. Prepared, starting, running, terminal and
unknown states have different meanings. Process liveness does not establish
productive computation. A missing terminal receipt is not a successful exit.

`practical.job.status` and `practical.job.collect` expose the native outcome,
available stdout/stderr tails, original offsets and file sizes. Use
`practical.file.read` when a further log/output window is needed. Elapsed
`systemd_service_wall_seconds` includes the native service lifecycle; it is
not a separately measured queue wait or program-only execution interval.

A scoped `receipt_ref` lets a later practical episode observe an original
execution from another episode. The binding verifies the saved receipt's scope,
requested job digest and resource kind. The receiver validates its own output
requirements against that original execution; it does not rewrite the closed
launch's actions or credit.

The caller's endpoint is either a usable job handoff or successful requested
job outputs with the declared predicates. A handoff can be complete while the
native job continues. For an output endpoint, successful return and file
presence alone may not establish exact result identity: use declared file-hash
predicates where needed. Preparation commands cannot self-declare completion.
Validated endpoint completion makes future expected credit exactly zero while
preserving the final actual gain; the configured controller owns continuation.

Native execution, resource and filesystem failures retain their specific
outcomes. Unknown or active work is never replaced. A later explicit
`practical.job.start` can name `retry_failed_execution_id` only for the exact
confirmed failed current execution; repairing preparation does not itself
authorize a replacement. No retry, timer, polling cadence or forced cancellation
is chosen by this library. Source rows L3–L5.

# Local handles, results and failures

The original requested job has a durable disk handle and systemd execution
identity. Recovery observes that handle; it does not repeat submission because
the episode or caller restarted. Prepared, starting, running, terminal and
unknown states have different meanings. Process liveness does not establish
productive computation. A missing terminal receipt is not a successful exit.

`practical.job.status` and `practical.job.collect` expose the native outcome,
available stdout/stderr tails, original offsets and file sizes. Use
`practical.file.read` when a further log/output window is needed. Elapsed
`systemd_service_wall_seconds` includes the native service lifecycle; it is
not a separately measured queue wait or program-only execution interval.

A scoped `receipt_ref` lets a later practical episode observe an original
execution from another episode. The binding verifies the saved receipt's scope,
requested job digest and resource kind. The receiver validates its own output
requirements against that original execution; it does not rewrite the closed
launch's actions or credit.

The caller's endpoint is either a usable job handoff or successful requested
job outputs with the declared predicates. A handoff can be complete while the
native job continues. For an output endpoint, successful return and file
presence alone may not establish exact result identity: use declared file-hash
predicates where needed. Preparation commands cannot self-declare completion.
Validated endpoint completion makes future expected credit exactly zero while
preserving the final actual gain; the configured controller owns continuation.

Native execution, resource and filesystem failures retain their specific
outcomes. Unknown or active work is never replaced. A later explicit
`practical.job.start` can name `retry_failed_execution_id` only for the exact
confirmed failed current execution; repairing preparation does not itself
authorize a replacement. No retry, timer, polling cadence or forced cancellation
is chosen by this library. Source rows L3–L5.

# Pairwise sequence and selected-read alignment

`sequence.align` compares the supplied query and reference sequences.
`reads.align` compares each explicitly selected original read with the supplied
reference, preserving separate results and failures. Choose protein, DNA or RNA
and local or global alignment in the actual input contract. These operations
run Biopython pairwise alignment through the bounded local execution binding.
They do not search a sequence database or select another resource.

Use local alignment to inspect matching regions and global alignment to compare
the complete supplied operands under the recorded scoring model. Retain the
actual matrix, match/mismatch and gap parameters with the result. RNA inputs
retain their declared molecule; the native alignment normalizes U to T.

The retained output includes both gapped strings and zero-based, half-open
coordinate paths. The numerical sheet distinguishes paired residues,
identical pairs, substitutions, gap columns and residues aligned to gaps.
`paired_identity` divides identical pairs by paired positions;
`alignment_identity` divides them by all alignment columns. Paired coverage
divides paired positions by the complete corresponding operand length;
aligned coverage also includes that operand's residues opposite a gap.
The sheet preserves each denominator. Literal equality of ambiguity symbols
does not resolve the underlying residue.

An explicit local no-alignment result has zero aligned positions and unknown
identity. Invalid geometry cannot provide positional coverage. Native alignment
scores are model-dependent scores, not probabilities of function. Return only
the requested numerical components and correspondence; complete strings and
sheets remain retained for later explicitly scoped use. Parsing and calculation
belong to the same selected result action and do not create additional turns.

# Sequence composition and original read quality

`sequence.inspect` measures the supplied sequence. `reads.inspect` measures
exactly the selected original reads and keeps each read's association with
its source member and original quality string. The latter is one selected
operation with separate per-read measurements, not a whole-library inference.

The input's declared molecule controls interpretation. DNA and RNA GC fraction
uses G+C divided by the number of unambiguous A/C/G/T or A/C/G/U symbols,
respectively. Ambiguity fraction uses ambiguous symbols divided by total
sequence length. The sheet retains counts and denominators. Protein and
unspecified-molecule inputs do not receive a nucleotide GC interpretation.
Alphabet compatibility does not classify a molecule or imply function.

Read quality requires the complete original quality string and declared
`phred33`, `phred64` or `solexa64` encoding. Do not guess encoding from printable
characters. The deterministic calculator reports mean Phred score, expected
error count, mean error probability and counts/fractions at explicit thresholds.
Phred error probabilities use 10**(-Q/10); Solexa values use their odds
conversion. Missing encoding, invalid characters or a sequence/quality length
mismatch leaves the affected quantities unavailable, not perfect or zero.

The complete quality distribution and inputs are retained so thresholds can
be recalculated without reacquiring data. Default Q20 and Q30 reports are
measurements, not acceptance gates. Return only requested measurements;
complete raw reads, quality strings and sheets remain outside model prompts.
